# Regulated output changes (ReARM Pro), record at RO-1

<!-- Generated by ReARM's regulated output record test. Do not edit: a changed copy fails the documentation image build. -->

ReARM Pro makes documents that a manufacturer hands to a regulator or keeps as the record of doing so, and applies rules that judge them. This page lists those outputs, gives identifiers that name parts of their state, and holds the change record: one entry for each change that moved an identifier or that its author recorded. It is written for the person who validates ReARM as software used in a quality system, as one input to the decision whether a validation made on an earlier release still covers what ReARM produces. It does not make that decision.

How to use it. When you validate, note the number of the last entry below. After an upgrade, read the entries above that number: each says which output changed, what changed and what to do. The release notes of a ReARM release name the entries the release adds under the heading `Regulated output changes`, or say that it adds no entry. No new entry means that no change was recorded. It does not mean that no output changed: the column `Not held by an identifier` says what can change without an entry.

A package version that is already Final keeps `internal/manifest.json` and every file the manifest names as they were made. The other files of its zip are written again at each download, by the release that serves the download: `internal/README.txt`, `internal/manifest.sha256`, `internal/zip-index.json`, the two files of the record of review, and the zip around them. An entry about one of these applies to an earlier package when it is downloaded again; every other entry describes what ReARM produces from the release that carries it.

What an entry rests on. An identifier marked computed is worked out from the code by a test of ReARM Pro, and the test fails while this record gives another value. An identifier marked raised is a constant its author changes by hand: the same test reads it, and nothing raises it when the output changes. An identifier marked declared is written into an entry by its author; for the three that name the pins of rebom, the service that merges release SBOMs and runs the checking engine, a check of ReARM compares the value with rebom's build files of the same commit at each push that changes them and at each release. A change that moves no identifier is recorded only if its author adds an entry; the column `Not held by an identifier` says what that covers. The values below are those of the ReARM Pro source this page was generated from. This record is not a validation of ReARM and not a statement that an output meets a regulator's expectations.

This record describes ReARM Pro. ReARM CE merges release SBOMs and runs the checking engine too, and is not covered by it.

## Outputs

| Output | What it is | Identifiers | Not held by an identifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Release SBOM | The merged SBOM of a release: the SBOM part of a package, an SBOM export and the aggregate SBOM published on TEA. | `merge-version`, `fda-recipe`, `rebom-engine`, `rebom-engine-image`, `rebom-tools` | What rebom, the service that runs the merge, adds of its own: its code around the merge, the runtime and the libraries it runs on. The support data added to the SBOM. A profile named `fda` that your organization stores replaces the built-in recipe and is yours. |
| Package zip | The zip of a Final version: the folders `fda/` and `internal/`, the file names, `internal/README.txt`, `internal/manifest.json`, `internal/manifest.sha256` and `internal/zip-index.json`. | `package-parts`, `package-readme`, `package-file-names`, `zip-container`, `manifest-version`, `manifest-form`, `zip-index-version`, `zip-index-form` | The name of a file for product names and versions other than the made-up ones, a README of a package that leaves parts out, a key of the manifest or the index when it is absent, and the values a key may take. |
| Generated documents | The vulnerability disclosure report (VDR), the VEX, the narrative, the software support addendum and the device software support statement, with the footer of the HTML documents. | `document-texts`, `support-documents-form` | The VDR and the VEX: only their fixed texts are held, nothing of how they are built. Of the addendum and the statement: what a release other than the made-up one would show, when a sentence is built in the code and not kept as a fixed text. The narrative is your organization's text under six lines of ReARM. |
| Record of review | `internal/record-of-review.json` and `internal/record-of-review.html`: who did what on a package version, and when. | `record-of-review-version`, `record-of-review-form` | The labels of the kinds of act, cause, capacity and state other than the made-up ones, and a key when it is absent. |
| Readiness rules | The rules a draft is checked against before Confirm and Finalize, as the Readiness rules page lists them. | `rule-set-version`, `readiness-rules`, `readiness-decisions` | A decision on a draft that is none of the cases ReARM keeps for the rules. |
| Check report | `check-report.json`, the stored check of a version: the pin of the release SBOM, two counts and the checking engine's report. | `check-report-version`, `rebom-engine`, `rebom-engine-image`, `rebom-tools` | What the report holds for the same SBOM, its keys among them, beyond its number and the pin of the engine that makes it. |
| FDA checker rules | The checks of the engine that judges a release SBOM, as the FDA checker rules page lists them. | `rebom-engine`, `fda-checker-rules` | A decision of the engine that no statement of its list covers, the engine's version (a check report names the engine that made it), and whether this page is the list of the engine that `rebom-engine` names: both move under one entry, and no check compares the two. |
| Review confirmation | The statement a person confirms at Confirm and at Finalize, as an act records it. | `confirmation-statement-id`, `confirmation-statement-version`, `confirmation-statement-text` | Whether the version was raised when the words changed: an act records the id and the version only, and the words have an identifier of their own. |

Not on this list: a draft and its zip (marked DRAFT, not for submission); the files your organization uploads, which a package carries as they are; a lifecycle events file (CLE), which no package kind lists; what ReARM shows on screen; the TEA API itself.

## Changes

The newest entry is the last.

### RO-1: First record

- Outputs: Release SBOM; Package zip; Generated documents; Record of review; Readiness rules; Check report; FDA checker rules; Review confirmation
- Kind of change: first record
- What changed: This is the first release of ReARM Pro with this record. Against the release before it every output listed here is new or changed: the release SBOM is merged otherwise (merge version 18 before), the manifest has more keys (manifest version 1 before), the generated documents changed, the FDA checker rules had no number, and the package zip, the record of review, the readiness rules, the check report and the confirmation statement did not exist.
- What to do: Validate the outputs you use from this release on, and note RO-1 as the entry you validated at. A package made by an earlier release keeps its manifest and the files the manifest names.
